text_fidelity_a:
Moorebot Scout - Tiny AI Camera Robot for Tech-Minded, Pets/Edlerly Watching/Security/Smart Home/Crawlspace Inspection, 1080P, Auto Patrol, Nightvision, Track Option, Indoor (2023) My office was just moved to a new building that as yet has no cameras inside...Well...Sort of. Now I've got Scout here to take care of business. It's like a Ring doorbell on wheels.

I'm having a lot of fun controlling it manually from home. It connects to the wifi at work and I check in on things using the app. It's working very well and seems to hold a signal about 250kbps. 1080p recordings look fine. For myself, the night vision works a charm. It's clear enough to identify people, and that's all that matters. Plus, driving it around my office while I'm in bed is pretty cool, too.

Battery takes about three hours to charge out of the box and it lasts about 2hr running around the building before it goes back to the base. Most recent firmware update makes that process significantly faster, too. If you've got it on a slick surface, it might have some trouble, but it'll get plugged in eventually. Says battery runs out after an hour using only night vision, but you can set that to automatic in the app.

Around the house, the little noises are kinda neat, but for use as security, that'd be something to disable....except the alarm. That's something to keep on in case you need to scare someone off. Recording all that stuff and saving files to the phone is a plus.

I really like this little guy. It's definitely something you'll have to play around with, but it is a load of fun getting set up.
text_fidelity_b: Moorebot Scout - Tiny AI Camera Robot for Tech-Minded, Pets/Edlerly Watching/Security/Smart Home/Crawlspace Inspection, 1080P, Auto Patrol, Nightvision, Track Option, Indoor (2023)

This is, we both agree, the best kit we've put together. I think that the biggest selling point is that at the end, it looks like a toy, not a LEGO kit. When you have the arachnoid built, there are very few places where you can see the tell-tale pegs.

The kit comes with a few extras - a few minifigs, a small spider minion - but the kit is otherwise entirely made up of the arachnoid mech. Like other Monkie Kid sets, this one is somewhat light on additional characters as opposed to other sets LEGO has made in the past.

Overall, though, this is an impressive kit. It's not terribly challenging, it looks great, it moves well, and it's not particularly dainty to move around. Love it.

text_fidelity_a:
The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

My style is more along the lines of giving them art supplies and letting them create what they want, and honestly, that's what I'll always prefer for them. They really enjoy projects that have a somewhat defined end result sometimes, though, and so it's kits like this that come to my rescue. Thankfully, they still get to be a bit creative with these projects, and while end results might look similar for many children, they probably won't look just alike.

There are 16 projects within this box, with lots and lots of little pieces. The supplies are all separated into different bags, and there are even extra bags for me to divide out some of the supplies. I could turn my children loose with everything and see what they come up with, but I prefer separating each project(at least for the most part), so that my children can choose which one they want to do, and not worry about running out of supplies before all the project are finished. Between my 3 children, I'll get 5 rainy days out of this box, with one extra. (I can't beat that!) ;) Plus, the included finger crayons can be used after all the projects are finished.

This is a really nice box of crafts. Especially if you're like me, and don't do so well with organized crafts, this is an excellent way to give your children some fun with crafts.

The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) This game is addicting and so much fun for ages 10+. The teenagers at the summer camp I run especially found it fun.

The short version of how it works: Everyone gets an identity (spy or resistance member). Spies get to see who the other spies are, resistance members are clueless. You take turns choosing people to go on missions hoping that you don't have a spy among your group. Everyone on that mission turns in a pass or fail card. The spies are trying to get missions to fail, and resistance members are trying to pass the missions. You have 5 mission rounds to battle it out.

The first round or two playing with new people is always pretty quiet and awkward, but once everyone catches on to how to play, and opens up the game becomes a blast! It's been a great ice breaker for us, and it's got the kids talking and making friends with each other. All while being deceitful, calling others out for being spies, but overall having fun!

It's definitely more fun the more people you have, but it's still playable with only 5.
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5 This is a precious little game that I imagine young children will long remember.

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5

text_fidelity_a:
Magnatab — A to Z Uppercase — Activity for Fun and Learning — Sensory Activity — Ages 3+ SUMMARY
This is a fun and clever toy that can really help kids learn their letters. It certainly captures their attention initially but after 2 days it doesn't seem to be interesting any more. For longer term interest I would suggest the Magnatab that is more of a doodle pad. It is a durable toy and looks like it would stand up in a classroom. However, the magnetic stylus is not attached to the rest of the toy and could very easily be lost.

FULL REVIEW

KIDS COMMENTS
My kids want you to know that they like the sound that the beads make when they pop up and they like how the beads "appear" when they put the magnet to them.

FORM - A+
This toy is nicely sized. It perfectly fits in an adult or child's lap and has a nice curved edge around the back that makes it nice to hold. The letters are nicely sized and spaced on the board. The stylus is comfortable in the hand and easy for little fingers to hold without being bulky. The slot that the stylus fits into for storage is super clever and has a magnet that holds it in place. In concept and usage I like this better than a stylus attached with a string or plastic loop. However, practically, I'm afraid that the stylus will be lost since it is not attached to the rest of the toy.

DURABILITY - A-
I immediately gave this toy to 4 children, ages 7-18 months. They loved it for the first two days. It got tossed, sat on, fought over, and played with pretty constantly. The only problem that I saw was some faint smudging of the black print on the Magnatab. It looks like some excess toner being wiped or smudged across the surface. However, none of the print has come off yet and the direction arrows are still nice and dark. I believe this toy is durable enough to stand up in an education environment. Other than the stylus issues described above this toy would be a good investment for a school or day care.
text_fidelity_b: Magnatab — A to Z Uppercase — Activity for Fun and Learning — Sensory Activity — Ages 3+

3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide The 3Doodler Create + is both a toy and an artist's tool. While trying it out the hours flew by, I felt like a little kid playing with new toys on Christmas morning. Despite the fact that it will take a lot of practice before I can make anything useful or artistic, I'm having a blast trying to learn how to make various shapes. The instructions are very basic, but the website has lots of hints, tips, projects, and stencils to download for free. There are quite a few YouTube videos as well.

As the packaging states, the tip gets incredibly hot. However, the pen's design makes holding it and using it comfortable without risk of a burn. There are 2 types of filaments in the kit; ABS and PLA.

PLA is made from sugarcane and cornstarch and is used for plastic cups, cutlery, and other food grade plasticware. It has a lower melting point and a slightly glossier finish but is not as strong as ABS.

ABS requires a higher melting point and has a chemical smell but it is stronger and less likely to break if dropped.

Cleaning it after use is easy. If there is still some of the plastic sticking out from the unheated end of the pen you simply tap one of the speed buttons twice and it goes in reverse. Once the filament clears the gear mechanism, which can be seen through a clear window, it's easy to pull out. If there is no plastic sticking out then simply use the rest of it up or the long tool can be used to push the remainder out once the tip is removed. The kit has tools to accomplish this and more. The website has good visual instruction for removing the plastic.

So far I wrote my dog's name. The second try was legible but more practice is needed. I then made a pyramid. Not too difficult but a bit rough...more practice needed. I have tried to make a long vertical spiral...haven't figured that out yet. I think it's best if I stick with 2 dimensional objects until I am better able to control the pen and it's flow. Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

text_fidelity_a:
Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

SmartLab Toys Squishy Human Body with 21 Removable Body Parts with Anatomy Book This product has the potential to be an incredible teaching tool which is why I initially purchased it. However, it is evident after ordering this item (even after a replacement of the original product that was initially delivered--replacement is shown in pictures above), that there are reoccurring issues with this item that are extremely problematic.

You can see how there are pieces of this product that come lodged incorrectly including the skull which does not stay in its designated hole. The large intestine looks like it's already been pulled apart by a child passed its point of stretch as it is extremely thin at the connection area.

Also--I if I as a teacher could not even put this item in full back together, I can only imagine how difficult this would be for a child of any age to maneuver as well.

If this company would just give more effort into putting out a quality product it would be extremely useful across-the-board and save them so much money in returns if they would just take the small effort to fix these ongoing issues that so many purchasers report.

I was able to get a 25% refund on my initial purchase with being able to keep the item as I explained I do not want to do a third replacement bit instead that I would rather just find a innovative way to make the issues I've experienced usable for teaching my students.

If you get this product don't settle for a poor quality item...they used to be made so well and now this company has made cheaply made pieces of it the regular. Stick to your guns on insisting on either a working product and/or a refund.

Wish you all the best with this item.

text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain My boys(3, 5, and 7) had fun with this kit, overall, but there's really not much to it.

Basically, you mix up cornstarch, gelatin(both provided), and water, through various steps, and then pour it into the provided molds. This project has to be done in several steps, with waiting periods in between. With my children being so young, the wait was annoying. Thankfully, we did the project on a day that it was beautiful outside, and there was plenty of play in between, so it could have been worse.

After the brain/eye has set up in the mold, you'll dump it out, and paint it. You get paint(food coloring) in the kit, and can mix it up to what colors you want. My children were disappointed that they couldn't get the colors to look as bright as they do in the pictures. I even helped with this attempt. The colors were just very dull, and our brain didn't look anywhere near how bright it was shown to be. I'd recommend using real paint, as opposed to food coloring. I think the results will be better.

The molds are reusable, so as long as you don't mind buying more gelatin and cornstarch, you can make as many brains and eye balls as you'd like.

Overall, this is a fun little experiment if you're studying brains or eyes. It's very simple, though, despite the several steps, which make it time consuming.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain

Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari Hasbro's new Elefun's Snackin Safari Game for children 3 and up has a wonderful concept for fun, if your child has a lot of patience. The game is made for 1 or 2 players. There are two elephant heads with handles connected to a long slinky trunk with a suction cup on the end. Included are 2 home base cards and 13 snack cards. The object of the game is to pick up a snack card with the suction cup, and there are 3 different ways to play the game.

The first way to play is to find the Golden Tutti Fruit Cake and be the winner. The second way is to collect all your matching colors to win and the third way is to get the most pairs of matching snacks to win. It sounds easy enough, until you realize that it takes a lot of patience to bounce the elephant's slinky trunk quickly and hard enough to actually suction a card to it. It could take 6 times or 60 times, as the slinky is a weak plastic one and the small suction cup needs to be pushed on a card to pick it up.

Surprisingly enough, the little ones loved the concept, but after a dozen tries to pick up a card, became frustrated. If Hasbro can tweak this game to make a stronger slinky and stronger suction cup, so the little ones can pick up a card after a few tries, this game would be a big hit. I hope Hasbro reads these reviews and makes this cute game less frustrating, as the kids will really enjoy it!

text_fidelity_a: Monterey LG8510 Lady Bug Lure, Pack of 3 I buy these lures each year ever since I learned that ladybugs like to cluster in small hollow space in houses. One year I had 1 exterior wall with over 1000 ladybugs crawling on it in the sunshine, a day later they were all gone and over the following weeks they started falling out of the cracks inside my house. Every morning as soon as the sun rose I would start finding them everywhere. I checked the internet and found the Ladybuglady who told me that ladybugs cluster in the late fall to stay warm through the winter. If they find a space like a house and a way in they will literally take over the sun side wall of the house. The way to avoid this was to build ladybug houses (similar to bird house but with smaller holes) and place them in your garden and orchards where the Ladybugs will benefit your plants (they eat aphids) and get these lures to draw them to the houses. Well for 2 years it has worked like a charm. No ladybugs in my houses and the trees in my orchard are doing very well.

text_fidelity_a:
eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." Anyways, the cards are really lovely and sturdy. They seem sort of indestructible because one of the kids I nanny is 18 months old and a total "rip things to shreds" sort and he wasn't even able to destroy one! They also wipe off nicely with a damp cloth.

Do consider using these for your own kids! You wont be sorry!
text_fidelity_b: eeBoo French Flash Cards

text_fidelity_a: KidKraft Deluxe Wooden Fire Rescue Play Set with Ambulance, Fire Truck, Helicopter, Firefighters, 27 Pieces, Gift for Ages 3+ The toy is well-designed and promises many hours of creative play for my fire-fighter enthusiast grandson. It was easy to put together, with excellent instructions. The construction seems sturdy. I didn't give it five stars because of several factors. I deducted one star for poor paint quality. There were scratches in the paint finish, and the worst were on the header with "Fire Station" painted on it, just where it will be the most visible. The paint seems very thin, and flaked areas look like they'll easily spread with use. In many places, the paint came off when I peeled the part-number stickers off. I deducted the second star because the accessories were not as advertised in the listing or the video. Missing were the doghouse; one of the basketball standards (two were shown; only one was included); the bathroom sink; and one firefighter (two were included; the description promises three). The firefighter's helmet makes it nearly impossible for him to fit through the holes to slide down the pole. The Dalmatian dog pictured was replaced by a brown dog, with a dog bed that he does not fit into, instead of the doghouse. The TV/bookcase console was replaced by a freestanding TV on a pole that is very unrealistic looking. The included accessories match the parts-list in the instruction booklet, so I know the omissions were not accidental.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Wooden Fire Rescue Play Set with Ambulance, Fire Truck, Helicopter, Firefighters, 27 Pieces, Gift for Ages 3+

ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner We received this toy tonight and my youngest daughter (5 years old) used all the paint making some really cool spin art for me. Overall, I think it is a wonderful activity for children that was surprisingly NOT messy. Of course, the "splash guard" that is included looks A LOT like trash (luckily they have a small sticker that tells you it is the splash guard and not to be thrown away).

It takes one "C" battery which we had on hand (luckily) and we were good to go. My daughter had a blast and once I showed her where to place the corners she had no problem doing it all on her own. The paper is like (black and white)card stock and even though it curls a bit at first after getting painted but eventually it lays down flat. We used both colors but only the white color works nicely. The black doesn't show the colors good and after the paint dries you can't hardly see it so do yourself a favor and use the white side. The only other problem I see is that the glitter tubes should have a shaker end since younger kids have real problems shaking anything out of an open tube.

I have a feeling we will be going get more paint (and paper) really soon because it was a hit with my daughters and we taped their art work to the computer cabinet.

Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity My grandson is almost three years old, and I thought he’d enjoy this toy...that was until I received it. Upon first inspection you notice a cheaply made zip-up half circle that opens to expose rivets that a child is supposed to insert the enclosed plastic big “buttons”. Let me just tell you that there’s no way that my grandson can attach these things to the mat - it took all my strength and dexterity to get one or two to pop in place. This is simply too difficult for a child of any age and not challenging but frustrating. Then there’s these cute little ocean-themed felt cut-outs that you’re supposed to “hook” around the installed buttons. They’re brightly colored and my grandson did enjoy taking them off and on the buttons for about 15 minutes. Then there’s a few pieces of string...some are about 4” long (too short to practice tying and really too short for a toddler to attempt to thread through four holes on the felt pieces) and others are about 6” long. ALSO, Within fifteen minutes of play my toddler was pulling on the buttons attempting to remove them and the rivets we’re poppong off and the mat was falling apart, not to mention the tiny metal circles all over the floor were now a choking hazard and the mat no longer works in the holes that lost the rivets.

Overall PROs- cute felt pieces that easily attach much like a button hole that toddler can practice with.
CONs-cheap plastic sewn mat, hard to attach buttons, useless strings, mat falling apart during first play.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity

Mega Construx Halo Kinsano Cyclops Raid This Halo Tank set is a very cool set for any fan of the games. It has a few small figures that look significantly more realistic than a LEGO dude, and he even has a little rocket launcher thing that he can hold. He's a little big to fit inside the vehicle, but you can just leave him attached to the top of the tank, and it looks just as good.

The Tank itself is very interesting. I haven't built all 20 combinations, but they appear to be a combination of different kinds of turrets and treads that, combined with one another, create all of the varieties. You'll use a substantial amount of the pieces to make each construction, so you'll never have enough to truly mix and match, but there are some parts of the assembly that carry over from adaptation to adaptation. Switching these out is easy enough, but it's certainly not plug-and-play.

So you can use it, of course, for the puzzle pieces… But you can also use it for things like pencils… Candies… Stamps… And so on. So it is certainly a multipurpose sort of wooden box. Though this puzzle has 150 pieces… Due to the fact that all of the pieces are very unique, and some of them are even of animals, this is not the easiest puzzle to put together. Which, I think is a nice thing. Some of the pieces are very small, so this is not the type of puzzle you will want to work around small children.

At the current price of twenty-five bucks this puzzle is a bit pricier than other options. If you look around, you will certainly find other puzzles for less… But… If what you really want is a dolphin puzzle, then this is a nice one.

Hot Wheels Race Crate with 3 Stunts in 1 Set Portable Storage Ages 6 to 10 Adult review: it's fast. So fast it's over before it starts. I was most interested in the 4 lane gravity drop and it works perfectly. People complaining cars won't loop may not be trying different cars. After picking different cars a few times I have several that loop correctly. The two that came with it also loop correctly. Some of the longer cars don't seem to make it.

This is one of the neatest designs I've ever seen from Hot Wheels. If you wanted the 6 lane kit that's over 200 dollars from scalpers now...this is a pretty great one to settle for. My only complaints on the gravity drop are it's so fast it's really hard to watch and if you're at the starting end...the large solid loop prevents you from seeing the cars until the hit the finish line. If the loop were clear that would be awesome. I also added some old '68 track and will add more....the cars clear the finish with lots of go power left. Add more track :)

I ended up liking the drag race configuration best with added track.

I believe it is sturdy and it's a pretty big track in any configuration. The fact it all folds into itself for storage is the truly awesome part. Room for several cars in there as well.

Good product for young and old Hot Wheels fans and I wish it had been cheaper but feel I got my money's worth. If kids don't lose any of the few loose pieces....I would imagine it will hold value.
